chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him, ‘Is intercourse disliked at any particular time among the times?’ He said, ‘Yes, it is disliked on a night in which the moon is eclipsed, on the day in which the sun is eclipsed, between sunset and the disappearance of the twilight, from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun, during the black, red, and yellow wind, and during an earthquake.’

And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم once spent a night with one of his wives, and the moon was eclipsed on that night, so nothing occurred from him. His wife said to him, ‘O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, is all this due to dislike?’ He said, ‘Woe to you, this event has occurred in the heaven, so I disliked to take pleasure and to enter into anything.’
And Allah, the Exalted, has indeed reproached a people and said: ‘And if they were to see a fragment from the sky falling, they would say: piled-up clouds.’
By Allah, no one has intercourse during these times that I have described, then is granted a child from that intercourse, while having heard this hadith, except that he will see what he dislikes.

key_terms.تَنْكَسِفُ: is eclipsed, referring to the sun
key_terms.ٱنْخَسَفَ: was eclipsed, referring to the moon

ai.seo_question: At what times is intercourse considered disliked in this hadith from Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that intercourse is disliked at certain times associated with cosmic or unsettling events, such as eclipses, specific periods of the day, unusual winds, and earthquakes. It cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and a Quranic passage to emphasize reverence at such moments. It also warns of an undesirable outcome for one who knowingly ignores this teaching.
